summary: Daniel A. Getz is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, also studying under Ying-shih Yü, Masaaki Chikusa, and Taryo Makita, and became an associate professor at Bradley University.

Daniel Aitken works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under Jay L. Garfield, having also studied under Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his doctoral degree from the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.
Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He held posts at Butler University, the University of Kansas, and Soka University.

Daniel Baum is an Indologist and linguist. He earned his BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and his doctorate at Leiden University (circa 2001–2006) under Alexander Lubotsky, having also studied under Saul Migron.
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He completed his Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Indiana University and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD under Victor H. Mair), he served as an associate professor at Cornell University.
Daniel Clarke Waugh is a historian of Central Asia. He earned a BA at Yale and graduate degrees at Harvard before joining the faculty at the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale, president of the University of California, founding president of Johns Hopkins University, and president of the Carnegie Institution and the American Oriental Society.
Daniel Cozort works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and taught at Bates College and Dickinson College.

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar of religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He served as a director of research at the CNRS, the University of Lille, and University Lille-III from circa 1985 to 2015.

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Harvard University and under traditional teachers in India. He spent his career at Harvard, serving as Wales Professor of Sanskrit from circa 1958 to 1983.

Daniel John Gogerly was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served with the Wesleyan Mission Press, the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society, the Central School Commission of Ceylon, and as president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka.
Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago. He taught for decades as a professor at the University of British Columbia.

Daniel M. Stuart is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt, he became an assistant professor at the University of South Carolina.
Daniel P. Brown specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Ngawang Wangyal around 1971. He served as a professor at Harvard University from circa 1980 to 2022.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his thesis at Florida State University under the supervision of Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.
Daniel Schlumberger was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the University of Strasbourg. He succeeded Joseph Hackin and later held a post at Princeton University from circa 1968 to 1972.

Daniel Sperber is a historian who studied at institutions including University College London. He held academic posts at Bar-Ilan University beginning around 1968 and at the Open University of Israel.
Daniel Stuart Capper, Jr. works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA and MA from the University of Virginia and his PhD from the University of Chicago.
